question: What is the motion of an object called when it travels along a circular path at a constant speed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uniform circular motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uniform circular motion** refers to the motion of an object traveling along a **circular path** with a **constant speed**.
 
• Even though the speed remains constant, the **direction of motion** continuously changes, resulting in a change in velocity. This change in velocity means that the object is accelerating, as acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity.
 
• The acceleration in uniform circular motion is directed towards the **center of the circular path**, and this is called **centripetal acceleration**.
 
• The force responsible for maintaining the circular motion is called the **centripetal force**, which acts perpendicular to the velocity of the object and towards the center of the circle.
 
• Examples of uniform circular motion include the motion of a satellite in orbit, the movement of a car around a circular track at constant speed, and the rotation of a fan blade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Non-linear motion:**

 
 
• This refers to motion that does not follow a straight line. It can involve changes in direction or curved paths. Examples include projectile motion and motion along parabolic or elliptical paths.
 
• It is not specific to circular motion and does not necessarily involve constant speed. Hence, this option is incorrect in the context of the question.
 
 
 
• **Linear motion:**
 
 
• Linear motion refers to motion in a straight line, such as a car moving on a straight road or a free-falling object under gravity.
 
• Since the question specifies motion along a circular path, this option is incorrect as circular motion is not linear.
 
 
 
• **Non-uniform circular motion:**
 
 
• Non-uniform circular motion occurs when an object moves along a circular path but with a **varying speed**.
 
• This is different from uniform circular motion, where the speed remains constant. Hence, this option is also incorrect in the context of the question.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Uniform Circular Motion:**
 
 
• The magnitude of velocity (speed) is constant.
 
• The direction of velocity changes continuously as the object moves along the circular path.
 
• The force responsible for maintaining the circular motion (centripetal force) is always directed towards the center of the circle.
 
• The acceleration acting on the object (centripetal acceleration) is also directed towards the center of the circle and is perpendicular to the velocity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Examples of Uniform Circular Motion:**

 
 
• The motion of planets around the sun in circular orbits.
 
• The movement of electrons around the nucleus in an atom (in simplified models).
 
• A vehicle moving at constant speed around a circular track.
 
• The rotation of a ceiling fan or a merry-go-round at a constant speed.
 
 
 
• **Equations for Uniform Circular Motion:**
 
 
• The centripetal force is given by: **F = (mv²)/r**, where *m* is the mass of the object, *v* is its speed, and *r* is the radius of the circular path.
 
• The centripetal acceleration is given by: **a = v²/r**.
 
• The time period of revolution (T) is the time taken to complete one full circle and is related to the speed and radius by **T = 2πr/v**.
